public_rationale: This is a rhetorical line about how LLMs make users feel. 'Affirming' could mean agreeing with the user or just paying attention to each message. 'Every single interaction' is plain hyperbole. 'Built to' is a claim about design intent across all LLMs. Each reading gives a different answer. A literal reading would be unfair to the speaker. A softened 'they tend to flatter users' reading would swap in a claim he did not make. Lab documents cut both ways: OpenAI admits a GPT-4o update became 'overly supportive' from training on user feedback, but it calls that a fault and rolled it back. With no plain reading to test, I do not score the claim.
limitations: A reader who takes 'affirming' to mean sycophancy could find partial support in sycophancy research, but only for a softer claim than the one written.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: LLMs are designed to focus on users and affirm every interaction.

statement.excerpt: LLMs are built to completely focus themselves on us and do so while affirming every single interaction.
statement.document_title: I Will Never Respect A Website

our_interpretation: The sentence is a rhetorical description of how chatting with an LLM feels. It sits in a passage about why people get attached to LLMs ('We love to be asked questions about ourselves').
'Affirming' has no fixed meaning here. It could mean agreeing with or validating the user (sycophancy), or only attentive acknowledgment of each message. These readings lead to different results.
'Every single interaction' is plainly hyperbole. A literal universal reading would be stretched against the speaker. A loose 'tends to validate' reading would add a softer claim he did not make.
'Built to' is about design intent across all LLMs. One lab's statements cannot settle that, and labs both reward user approval and say they train against sycophancy.
On reflection there is no single ordinary reading that can be tested without choosing for the speaker. So I do not score it.
criteria.support_condition: Not scored. Under a validation reading, support would need evidence that LLMs in general are designed or trained so that they validate users in essentially every exchange.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Not scored. Under a validation reading, contradiction would need evidence that mainstream LLMs are designed to, and do, routinely disagree with or correct users.

evidence.explanation: Shows that training on user feedback can make a model over-affirming, which fits the gist. But OpenAI calls this a mistake and says it rolled the update back, so it does not show LLMs are built to affirm every interaction. Context only.
